scope: Two calculations of one byte-identical SXI with IncludeFiles.INCFN=level1.mdb and identical MDBs: one process working directory contains level1.mdb; the other does not. Both must resolve the relative include under the SXI directory and produce matching native output.

manual.rule: If IncludeFiles.INCFN is not a full path, the application searches its current directory; file-dialog actions can change that directory.

frozen_commands: import and JSON-export one main SXI with relative IncludeFiles path
calculate SXI with process working directory equal run directory
export first JSON report and snapshot native outputs
calculate same SXI with frozen distinct process working directory lacking level1.mdb
export second JSON report and snapshot native outputs
acceptance_hypotheses: The main SXI JSON roundtrip preserves literal level1.mdb; other authored K04.var01 business tables and rows remain unchanged.

Both calculations of the same byte-identical SXI log the same absolute level1 and level2 MDB paths under the SXI directory, insert one IncludeFiles and one Station row, and have zero converter errors and accepted warnings.
Both calculations produce usable SXO files; their event streams and JSON reports are byte-identical to each other and accepted K04.var01 output. Binary SXO bytes may differ between runs.
GUI PID/start/session, host mutex, literal source/contract pins and original MDB association are preserved/restored.
gate: If the two arms differ in resolved include path, event stream, JSON report, or accepted parent event/report parity, this CLI relative-path claim is NO-GO. Both arms raw outcomes remain sealed even if rejected.
limitations: This shows that changing the CLI process working directory alone does not alter a relative top-level MDB include resolved under the SXI directory. A missing MDB can leave a session-0 process waiting for interaction; excluded v1.0.2 diagnostic records that behavior. This case does not establish GUI file-dialog/MRU directory changes, relative nested include resolution, SXI/OPI includes, arbitrary paths, or complete K04 coverage.
